preview_en:
Fresh from opening their UEFA Europa League campaign with a win on Wednesday, Sunderland could be brought straight back down to earth when they visit a Manchester City side with a 100% winning Premier League record this term.

Match News and Current Form

Despite playing out over half of the game with ten men, City edged a controversy-shrouded Manchester derby 1-0 to make it four wins from four in the Premier League under Enzo Maresca. The Cityzens could now open a top-flight campaign with five successive victories for only the fifth time in history, and they’re bound to be confident of doing so having won 20 of their last 30 Premier League games (D8, L2), with their 68 points gained therein level with reigning champions Arsenal. Returning to the Etihad should only reinforce belief too, with City winning 16 of their last 20 home league games (D3, L1), although their only defeat in that run did come on a Sunday!

After the euphoria of making their first European appearance in over 50 years in midweek, beating AZ Alkmaar 1-0, Sunderland now have to contend with balancing commitments. It’s a challenge that they’ll have to rise to if they’re to avoid the dreaded ‘second-season syndrome’, but if the valiant performance they displayed in last week’s 2-0 defeat to Arsenal is anything to go by, they don’t have to worry about that just yet. A repeat scoreline seems unlikely here given that the Black Cats have scored in eight successive top-flight away games, but goals won’t necessarily lead to success here as Sunderland haven't won any of their last 17 Premier League games against teams starting the round in the top two (D4, L13).

Head-to-Head History

Sunderland have never beaten Manchester City away from home in the Premier League (D2, L12) and are winless in nine top-flight meetings at any venue (D2, L7).

Hot Stats and Streaks

City have won the corner count in six of their last seven home league games.

All four of City’s league matches this term produced exactly three yellow cards.

Sunderland’s last six away league games saw both teams score.

Sunderland have won five of their last six Sunday-held Premier League matches (L1).

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Sunderland are the only side Erling Haaland has faced without scoring against in the Premier League, but having opened the scoring in City’s last three league games, he may not have to wait long here. These opponents haven’t been kind to Granit Xhaka down the years as he’s lost a career-high 16 H2Hs against City, collecting six yellow cards therein - only against three other sides has he received more.

After both received red cards last weekend, City’s Phil Foden and Sunderland’s Reinildo Mandava are suspended here.

Betting Analysis

Sunderland’s tendency to score on the road hints that Manchester City to win and both teams to score is the value pick here.

Author: Chris Wilson
